title: Claim
description: One factual claim occurrence found in the media: where it was observed (interval and modality), what was actually said or shown (original_text) and the normalized proposition the pipeline assessed. Normalization must not strengthen the claim. When a user or the pipeline later corrected the proposition, correction records who and what it replaced; the original wording is never rewritten. A claim says nothing about truth; see assessment.schema.json.

id.description: Stable within the investigation across report versions.

occurrence_id.description: Identifies this appearance of the proposition in the media. Repeated statements of the same proposition are separate occurrences; the evaluation contract uses the same notion.

interval.description: Where the occurrence is in the media, on the capture timebase for the live overlay or the media timebase for a shared video.

original_text.description: The words as transcribed or read on screen, including hedges, negation and attribution.

proposition.description: Normalized meaning that was assessed. Preserves negation, quantities, units, dates, attribution and uncertainty.

correction.description: Null when the proposition is the pipeline's original extraction.

corrects_occurrence_id.description: Earlier occurrence corrected by this later appearance. Both original appearances remain in this and prior immutable reports.

superseded_by_occurrence_id.description: Later correcting occurrence that supersedes this interpretation. A superseded occurrence must not retain an assessment in the reconciled version.

interpretation.description: Optional source-grounded extraction metadata. Absent on older reports. Eligibility is not an assessment or truth verdict. Character offsets reference upstream observation text; the claim interval remains its coarse observation envelope.

source_ref.description: Half-open character offsets with start_char < end_char, validated against the exact supplied observation by the extraction stage.

interpretation.description: Normative judgments and questioned/hypothetical scenarios cannot be factually eligible. Quoted-not-endorsed cannot carry endorsed commitment. Readers preserve unknown enums as unknown, never as eligibility.

superseded_proposition.description: The proposition this correction replaced, kept so the change is attributable and reversible.
